EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The United States has declared an "ECONOMIC D-DAY" against Iran, initiating what President Trump termed the "most crushing economic operation" in history, threatening severe financial repercussions for any country providing support to Tehran. This declaration follows reports of a secret US military-controlled shipping corridor established in the Strait of Hormuz, which now facilitates the passage of approximately 10 million barrels of oil daily. Simultaneously, Israel has conducted significant military operations in Gaza, Syria, and Lebanon, targeting Hamas commanders and Turkish deployment plans, escalating regional tensions while facing international condemnation for settlement expansion.

IRAN
President Trump announced the "most crushing economic operation" against Iran, asserting that Iran's navy and air force are destroyed, military factories are in ruins, and its currency is worthless. Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed these claims as a distraction from America's internal economic problems. The IRGC Spokesman, Brigadier General Mohsen Mohebi, warned that Iran would use "more destructive weapons" if a new war erupts. Iran executed a foreign national named Qaaem Hosseini, convicted for involvement in anti-regime riots in Isfahan. An Iranian MP, Ebrahim Rezaei, suggested withdrawing from the NPT in response to US economic pressure. Press TV reported that 18 US troops were killed and 757 wounded during the "US war on Iran." Reconstruction of the US-bombed Gachin 2 Bridge in southern Iran is 80% complete. A fire involving two tanker trucks broke out at the kerosene loading area of Tehran Oil Refinery. The US military claims its strikes have degraded Iranian radar and maritime surveillance in the Strait of Hormuz, and US forces intercepted eight Iranian drones and two cruise missiles this week in the area. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf visited Iraq to enhance judicial and legal cooperation, and Iran began transferring oil to Turkey and Afghanistan via railway from Kermanshah.

ISRAEL
Israeli forces conducted multiple operations: in Gaza, four Hamas Nukhba Force commanders from the Beit Lahia Battalion (Muhammad Hamdi Ahmed al-Masri, Samad Samir Harb Abu Jabal, Muhammad Attar, and Muhammad Fathi Hussein Nasser) were eliminated in a strike in Shanti. A police station in Gaza City was struck, killing nine and wounding 15, with at least four Hamas military wing operatives and one Popular Resistance Committees member present. A Hamas company commander involved in the October 7 onslaught was killed in Nuseirat. Paratrooper combat teams destroyed terror infrastructure and five launch pits. The IDF Chief of Staff, Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, visited the Israeli-held buffer zone in southern Syria, affirming that Israel would not allow hostile forces to establish themselves along its borders. Israeli warplanes and artillery struck Kafr Rumman, Tallat al-Dabsha, and the Ali al-Taher heights in southern Lebanon, described as a "fire siege" to isolate Hezbollah operatives. In the West Bank, extensive exercises were conducted in the Menashe and Yehuda Brigades, simulating multi-front scenarios. Prime Minister Netanyahu stated Israel would not tolerate a Turkish military presence in southern Syria, emphasizing a message of "Don't" followed by the Abu al-Duhur airbase strike. Defense Minister Yisrael Katz publicly mocked Turkish President Erdogan for "dangerous adventures" in Syria. The Israeli Prime Minister's Office denied authorizing an international force in Gaza, reiterating that no reconstruction would occur before Hamas is fully disarmed. Australia summoned Israel's ambassador, expressing anger over the IDF's decision not to prosecute anyone for the 2024 killing of seven World Central Kitchen aid workers in Gaza, including Australian Zomi Frankcom. The IDF admitted its forces fired on the vehicle carrying 5-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza in January 2024 and has opened a criminal investigation. The UK and Germany condemned Israel's decision to proceed with the E1 settlement project in the West Bank, with the UK threatening to respond in the coming weeks and summoning the Israeli envoy. Naftali Bennett, former Prime Minister, proposed a new security doctrine including targeting Iran for Hezbollah attacks, declaring Qatar an enemy state, and replacing Turkish and Qatari involvement in Gaza with Egypt. Over 107,000 passengers experienced delays at Ben Gurion Airport. A pregnant woman died at Soroka hospital from a rare complication, with the fetus also lost. A 60-year-old Tel Aviv resident was arrested for looting a war-damaged apartment.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli paratrooper combat teams destroyed a Hamas terror infrastructure and five launch pits in Gaza. Humanitarian conditions in Gaza are dire, with remaining water services reportedly near total collapse. Pro-Palestine groups in the UK formally requested government intervention against the "Gaza genocide," citing Israeli restrictions on aid. Hamas condemned recent Israeli strikes, which targeted commanders and a police station, calling on international mediators to intervene immediately to "protect the agreement from collapse." The Israeli Prime Minister's Office clarified that the political echelon has not approved the entry of an international force into Gaza and stated there would be no reconstruction before Hamas is fully disarmed. Settlers reportedly torched a house in Beit Amra near Hebron. A wildfire spread towards the Apheka settlement in southern Mount Hebron, prompting evacuations and closure of Road 60.

LEBANON
Israeli warplanes and artillery struck Kafr Rumman, Tallat al-Dabsha, and the Ali al-Taher heights in southern Lebanon. These strikes were reported as a "fire siege" around the Ali al-Taher ridge to isolate Hezbollah militants in an underground facility. Palestinian media reported two people killed and several injured by unexploded Israeli ordnance in southern Lebanon, attributing it to Israeli ceasefire violations.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Israel conducted airstrikes on the Abu al-Duhur military airbase in Idlib province, stating that Turkey was planning to deploy forces there. Turkey's Defense Ministry denied any Turkish military delegation was present and condemned Israel's actions as "reckless attacks." Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shibani confirmed prior discussions with Israel about Turkish presence but accused Israel of reneging on commitments in an American-brokered agreement. IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir visited the Israeli-held buffer zone in southern Syria, warning against hostile forces establishing themselves on Israel's borders. Reuters reported that Mossad chief Roman Gofman spoke with Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shibani on August 14 regarding Turkey's military presence. Lebanon extradited former Major-General Adel Issa, a high-ranking officer of the Assad regime, to Syria, where he faces charges of premeditated murder and other crimes. Iraqi Popular Mobilization Units (PMU) head Faleh al-Fayyadh stated that over 100 PMU members were martyred and dozens injured in the "war on Iran," with over 100 PMU headquarters bombed. He stressed PMU commitment to the Iraqi Prime Minister's directives and its national role, despite threats from armed groups close to Tehran. Iraqi Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf met with Iraqi judicial and government leaders in Baghdad to bolster bilateral cooperation, emphasizing Iraq's sovereignty and interest in oil exports via Hormuz. Iran commenced oil transfer by railway from Kermanshah to Turkey and Afghanistan.

GULF STATES
The United Arab Emirates announced the suspension of all financial and economic transactions with Iran, citing recent Iranian missile launches towards the Strait of Hormuz and weeks of US pressure to tighten oversight of Iranian financial networks. This move, while viewed as a gradual escalation rather than a complete break, could significantly reduce Iran's access to foreign currency. Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan reiterated the Kingdom's commitment to diplomatic solutions, dialogue, and peaceful means, emphasizing the importance of freedom of navigation in international waterways and maritime security. Kuwait's Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces met with his US counterpart at the Pentagon to discuss strengthening military cooperation. Oman's Foreign Minister affirmed that safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz is integral to regional security. The US military has established a "secret" shipping corridor in the southern Strait of Hormuz, with 15-20 tankers transiting nightly, moving approximately 10 million barrels of oil daily, roughly half the pre-war volume. This operation was enabled by US strikes that degraded Iranian radar and maritime surveillance, with US aircraft providing defense against Iranian drones and cruise missiles. President Trump asserted that the US has "complete control" over the Strait of Hormuz. Naftali Bennett proposed designating Qatar as an "enemy state" and removing it from activities in the Gaza Strip.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US "ECONOMIC D-DAY" on Iran**: President Trump announced the "most crushing economic operation" against Iran, threatening severe economic consequences for any nation providing a "lifeline" to Tehran.
2.  **UAE Suspends Financial Ties with Iran**: The United Arab Emirates suspended all financial and economic transactions with Iran, following US pressure and alleged Iranian missile launches near the Strait of Hormuz.
3.  **Secret US Shipping Corridor in Hormuz**: The US military established a covert shipping corridor in the southern Strait of Hormuz, allowing 15-20 tankers to transit nightly, transporting approximately 10 million barrels of oil daily under US air defense.
4.  **Israeli Strikes in Gaza**: Israeli forces killed four Hamas Nukhba Force commanders in Shanti/Beit Lahia and struck a police station in Gaza City, killing nine and wounding 15, while Hamas called for mediator intervention to protect the ceasefire.
5.  **Israeli Strike on Syrian Airbase**: Israel bombed the Abu al-Duhur airbase in Syria, stating it targeted Turkish deployment plans, prompting a warning from Israeli Defense Minister Katz to Erdogan.
6.  **Israeli Chief of Staff in Southern Syria**: IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir visited southern Syria, reiterating Israel's commitment to prevent hostile forces from establishing themselves on its borders.
7.  **Israel Admits Role in Hind Rajab's Death**: The Israeli military acknowledged its forces fired on the vehicle carrying 5-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab in January 2024 and opened a criminal investigation.
8.  **International Condemnation of E1 Settlement**: The UK and Germany condemned Israel's planned E1 settlement construction, with the UK threatening sanctions and summoning the Israeli envoy.
9.  **IRGC Threatens "More Destructive Weapons"**: IRGC Spokesman Mohsen Mohebi warned that Iran would use "more destructive weapons" if a new war breaks out.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are significantly high following President Trump's declaration of "ECONOMIC D-DAY" against Iran and his consideration of "intensive strikes" should economic pressure fail. Iran's IRGC Spokesman's threat of employing "more destructive weapons" in a new conflict further signals potential for escalation. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, where a US-controlled shipping corridor operates amidst degraded Iranian surveillance and intercepted Iranian drones/missiles, creating a direct confrontation risk. The Israeli military's aggressive posture in Gaza, Syria (against perceived Turkish threats), and southern Lebanon (targeting Hezbollah) maintains a high level of regional instability. Hamas's call for international intervention regarding Israeli strikes in Gaza indicates the fragility of any existing ceasefire. Houthi movements in Yemen, reportedly preparing for escalation with Saudi Arabia, could further broaden the conflict. Iran's consideration of targeting US military bases in Southeastern Europe in response to war expansion suggests a wider geographic scope for potential conflict.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US has intensified its economic campaign against Iran with the "ECONOMIC D-DAY" declaration, freezing talks, and operating a secret shipping corridor in the Strait of Hormuz. US officials reported intercepting eight Iranian drones and two cruise missiles this week. The Pentagon announced 18 US troops killed and 757 wounded in the "war on Iran." The UAE responded to US pressure and alleged Iranian missile launches by suspending all financial and economic deals with Iran. Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan emphasized diplomacy and maritime security. Kuwait's Chief of Staff met with his US counterpart to enhance military cooperation. Oman's Foreign Minister stressed the importance of safe passage in the Strait of Hormuz. The UK and Germany condemned Israel's E1 settlement project, with the UK summoning the Israeli envoy and threatening sanctions. France expelled two Iranian diplomats in retaliation for Iran's earlier expulsion of two French cultural attachés. Russia launched a large-scale missile and drone attack on Ukraine, causing 12 deaths and 33 injuries in Kyiv, and announced downing 726 Ukrainian drones, with a Romanian drone explosion reported on its territory. Russia also imposed fuel restrictions due to Ukrainian attacks. China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi urged the US to abandon its hostile policy towards North Korea and warned Japan against nuclear armament. Australia summoned Israel's ambassador to express anger over the closure of the World Central Kitchen aid worker killing investigation in Gaza. Colombia and Israel agreed on mutual visa exemptions starting September 1. North Korea launched 10 short-range ballistic missiles, its third such launch in two weeks. South Korea estimated North Korea possesses 80-120 nuclear warheads, differing from Trump's figure of 57, and rejected the deployment of US tactical nuclear weapons.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Reporting reveals several contradictions and unverified claims. Regarding the Strait of Hormuz, President Trump claims "complete control" while a US official cited by Axios states the IRGC does not control the Strait, and Iranian sources discuss collecting revenue from it. Turkish and Syrian officials deny a Turkish military presence at the Abu al-Duhur airbase, despite Israeli claims of targeting Turkish deployment plans. There is a discrepancy in estimates of North Korea's nuclear warhead count, with Trump stating 57 and South Korea's Defense Minister estimating 80-120.

Unverified claims include the Al-Akhbar newspaper's report (Hezbollah-affiliated) on Houthis preparing for a ground operation against Saudi Arabia, and reports of Iraqi PMU members killed and headquarters bombed during a "war on Iran," a term whose scope is not fully clarified by other sources. Reuters reported a phone call between Mossad Chief Roman Gofman and Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shibani prior to an Israeli strike, which was confirmed as a "talk" by the Syrian FM, but Gofman's identity was not specified by the Syrian side, and the source differs slightly on the date.

Propaganda indicators are evident in the strong, declarative language used by President Trump regarding Iran's military and economy, and by Iranian officials dismissing US claims as distractions. Hamas's call for mediators to "protect the agreement from collapse" after Israeli strikes in Gaza is also a clear messaging effort. Omid Dana's channel frequently features highly opinionated and sensationalized content, such as referring to individuals as "clowns" and making unconfirmed claims about the financial state of the Iranian military, which should be viewed with caution.

Reporting gaps include specific details of the alleged Iranian missile launches that prompted the UAE's suspension of financial ties, the full scope and terms of the prior agreement between Israel and Syria that the Syrian FM accused Israel of violating, and more precise information on the "US war on Iran" that reportedly resulted in US casualties. The exact nature and dates of the US-Israel strikes that degraded Iran's radar capabilities are also not fully detailed.
